source_text: XIV. Sed enim Montanus corpore et mente robustus, quamquam ante martyrium gloriosus quicquid semper veritas postularet constanter et fortiter dixerit sine ulla exceptione personae, tamen de martyrio proximo crescens prophetica voce clamabat: Sacrificans diis eradicabitur nisi domino soli. et hoc frequenter iterabat, insinuans et inculcans non licere deserto deo ad simulacra et manufacta figmenta accedere. haereticorum quoque superbiam et improbam contumaciam retundebat, contestans eos ut vel de copia martyrum intelligerent ecclesiae veritatem, ad quam redire deberent; deinde lapsorum abruptam festinantiam. negotiationem pacis ad plenam paenitentiam et Christi sententiam differebat, nec non integros quoque ad tutelam integritatis exhortans: State fortiter, fratres, et constanter militate, dicebat. habetis exempla, nec vos perfidia lapsorum destruat ad ruinam, sed nostra tolerantia magis aedificet ad coronam. virgines quoque singulas admonebat ut sanctitatem suam tuerentur. generaliter omnes docebat ut praepositos venerarentur. praepositis quoque ipsis concordiam pacis insinuans, nihil esse melius aiebat, quam praepositorum unanimem voluntatem. tunc et plebem posse ad sacerdotum obsequia provocari et ad vinculum dilectionis animari, si rectores plebis pacem tenerent. hoc esse propter Christum pati, Christum etiam exemplo sermonis imitari, et probationem maximam fidei. o exemplum grande credendi!
thought_title: Montanus preaches against idols and division on the way to die
orientation: The editor completing the account describes what Montanus said as he went to execution after the other confessors.
pass_a_gloss: But Montanus, strong in body and in mind, although before his suffering already honored, in that he had always said constantly and bravely whatever truth demanded without any exception of person, yet growing from his near suffering cried out with a prophetic voice: He who sacrifices to gods will be rooted out unless to the Lord alone. And he repeated this frequently, intimating and impressing that with God abandoned it is not permitted to go to images and inventions made by hand. He also beat back the pride and shameful stubbornness of breakaway Christians, calling them to witness that they should understand the truth of the church at least from the abundance of martyrs, to which they ought to return; then the abrupt hastiness of those who gave in under pressure. He put off the negotiation of peace to full repentance and to the judgment of Christ, and exhorting even those who are whole toward the guarding of wholeness: Stand bravely, brothers, and serve as soldiers constantly, he said. You have examples, and let not the treachery of those who gave in under pressure destroy you to ruin, but let our endurance rather build you up to a crown. He also admonished each maiden to guard her holiness. In general he taught all to revere the leaders. Also pressing upon the leaders themselves the unity of peace, he said nothing to be better than the united will of the leaders. Then also the people could be called forth to obedience to the priests and be encouraged to the bond of love, if the rulers of the people kept peace. This is to suffer for the sake of Christ, also to imitate Christ by example of speech, and the greatest proof of faith. O great example of believing!

pass_b_english: But Montanus was strong in body and mind. Even before his martyrdom he had won glory, for he always said whatever the truth demanded, firmly and boldly, without favoring any person. Now he grew greater as his martyrdom drew near, and he cried out with a prophetic voice: "He who sacrifices to gods will be rooted out unless to the Lord alone" (Exodus 22:20). He repeated this again and again, pressing and driving home that once God is abandoned, no one is permitted to turn to images and figures made by hands.

He also beat back the pride and shameless defiance of breakaway Christians, calling on them to recognize from the very number of martyrs the truth of the Church, to which they ought to return. Then he checked the headlong haste of those who gave in under pressure. He put off their bargaining for peace until full repentance and the judgment of Christ. He also urged those who still stood whole to guard their wholeness. "Stand firm, brothers, and serve steadfastly as soldiers," he said. "You have examples before you. Do not let the treachery of those who gave in under pressure drag you down to ruin, but let our endurance build you up toward the crown."

He urged each virgin separately to guard her holiness. As a rule he taught everyone to honor their leaders. To the leaders themselves he pressed the unity of peace, saying nothing is better than leaders of one mind. Only then, he said, could the people be stirred to obey the priests and be quickened into the bond of love, if the rulers of the people kept peace. This is what it means to suffer for Christ, to imitate Christ even by the example of speech, and it is the greatest proof of faith. O great example for belief!
notes: The clause deinde lapsorum abruptam festinantiam stands without a verb in the given source; glossed as a fragment and the next clause supplies the verb differebat.
